Implemented via specs/013-inherited-ira-edge-cases (shared with rp-c8b/rp-l4d), citing IRS Pub. 590-B (2025) pp.8-11 directly. Non-spouse EDB: annual divisor via 'longer of' beneficiary-vs-owner life expectancy when post-RBD (decrement-by-1 method), beneficiary-only when pre-RBD/Roth. Spouse EDB: divisor recalculated fresh every year (not decremented) + delayed start until the year the owner would have reached RBD when pre-RBD (reuses rmd.py's own RMD_START_AGE). Minor-child EDB: same non-spouse divisor formula, but depletion_deadline_year converts to majority_year+10 once they turn 21 (IRS's own age-21 majority rule for this purpose), computed once at resolution time from the beneficiary's own current_age. A true (non-minor) EDB gets a far-future sentinel deadline (no 10-year clock of their own). beneficiary_classification blocking flag removed; closed a pre-existing gap by adding a new trust_or_entity blocking flag (newly reachable now that classification alone no longer blocks). Filed rp-kn5 separately: same primary source suggests the ALREADY-SHIPPED non-EDB post-RBD divisor (012, unchanged here) may also need this 'longer of' comparison -- deliberately not bundled into this scope-boundary work. 12 new unit tests + parametrized BFF-level end-to-end regression tests + updated Scenarios page/Instructions copy. Full suite: 310 (root) + 61 (bff) + 99 (streamlit) passed.
